articles.title: Zion Williamson Calls Out Pelicans After Loss to Nets, 'Go Look Yourself in the Mirror'
articles.summary: Zion Williamson didn't hide his frustration following the New Orleans Pelicans' 145-111 loss to the Brooklyn Nets on Wednesday night.
articles.body:
Zion Williamson didn't hide his frustration following the New Orleans Pelicans' 145-111 loss to the Brooklyn Nets on Wednesday night.

Speaking to reporters after the loss, Williamson called out everyone on the Pelicans to "go look yourself in the mirror" to figure out what went wrong in another blowout loss:

"As men we have to, as a unit, players, coaches, everybody, you have to go look yourself in the mirror when you by yourself and say, did I do everything that I needed to do for my team? Did I do — was I in the gaps on defense? Was I a low man when I was supposed to? Did I get out there and contest shots to make it tough on them? Did I do everything I needed to do? Did I give in real effort? That's what everybody has to do."

Williamson also called the Pelicans' performance "unacceptable."

The 145 points scored by the Nets is tied with the Miami Heat for the most by a team in a game so far this season. Brooklyn put up at least 38 points in three of the four quarters.

Even when the Nets were held to just 24 points in the third quarter, New Orleans' offense failed to take advantage because it only put up 15 points.

Brooklyn shot 57 percent overall and 20-of-41 from three-point range. The Pelicans have allowed opponents to shoot better than 50 percent from the field six times in 12 games this season.

This loss paired with Monday's 138-87 defeat against the Golden State Warriors means the Pelicans have been outscored by 85 points in their last 96 minutes of game time.

New Orleans has given up at least 130 points five times in 12 games, including each of the last three. The Pelicans are responsible for four of the six highest-scoring games by an opposing team.

The Pelicans have lost four straight games after a decent 4-4 start. They have the fifth-worst defensive rating and s ixth-worst net rating this season.

New Orleans has played the last two games without Trey Murphy III due to a knee injury. He won't solve all of the defensive issues on his own, but his size and versatility creates problems for opposing teams.

We will find out if the Pelicans take Williamson's words to heart on Friday when they host the Memphis Grizzlies in an NBA Cup game at Smoothie King Center.

articles.title: WNBA Draft 2027 Lottery Odds Revealed for JuJu Watkins Sweepstakes as Teams Eye No. 1 Pick
articles.summary: The Houston Comets may have a new franchise cornerstone as they embark on their H-Town revival.
articles.body:
The Houston Comets may have a new franchise cornerstone as they embark on their H-Town revival.

The Comets and Toronto Tempo have the joint-best odds (32.9 percent) of landing the No. 1 overall pick in the 2027 WNBA draft.

That could mean having the opportunity to land USC star JuJu Watkins. The senior guard went first overall in Bleacher Report's 2027 mock .

Watkins missed the entire 2025-26 season while recovering from a torn ACL. She hasn't lost a step so far after making her return. Through the Trojans' first three games, she's averaging 24.3 points, 8.3 rebounds, 4.7 assists and 3.7 steals.

With the NCAA's five-year eligibility rules in place, Watkins and nearly all of her draft-eligible peers could opt to stay in school for another season. Salaries in the WNBA are higher than ever, but it could prove more financially advantageous thanks to NIL endorsements to stick around in college.

Assuming she declares, Watkins is the heavy favorite to go first overall.

Getting the No. 2 or 3 pick will be a nice consolation prize, given the talent that should be available.

Texas forward Madison Booker was a first-team All-American in each of the last two years. For her career, she has put up 17.2 points and 6.1 rebounds while shooting 47.9 percent from the field. Booker is a plus defender and an elite mid-range scorer who will make an immediate impact in the WNBA.

Notre Dame guard Hannah Hidalgo is a two-way terror on the perimeter. Going back to the 1987-88 season, her 496 career steals are eighth all time in Division I, and she boasts a 24.0-point scoring average.

LSU guard Mikaylah Williams is one of the best shooters in the class. She has a 39.8 percent career clip from beyond the arc. The 6'0" playmaker can help to facilitate the offense as well, dishing out an average of 3.4 assists per contest.

From a draft perspective, Watkins will command a lot of the spotlight and rightfully so. She's not the only prospect with All-Star potential, though.

The WNBA will hold its draft lottery on Sunday at 7:30 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Naz Reid Trade Addressed by NBA Insider as Potential Changes to Hornets' Roster Eyed
articles.summary: With the Charlotte Hornets building for the future, veteran center Naz Reid could once again be utilized as a trade chip.
articles.body:
With the Charlotte Hornets building for the future, veteran center Naz Reid could once again be utilized as a trade chip.

The Athletic's Jon Krawczynski suggested Tuesday on his podcast "the possibilities of Naz Reid getting traded again are very high" (20:53 mark).

"This is a roster that I think is going to change over quite a bit over the next couple of years as the Hornets look for the right combination of people to really vault what they hope is contention," the NBA insider said. "I think you can say that Brandon Miller and Kon Knueppel are gonna be there. Beyond that, who knows?"

How the Pistons Can Elevate as a Contender 🏀

Krawczynski elaborated that the change of scenery may have adversely impacted Reid.

The 27-year-old built a strong connection with the Minnesota Timberwolves and their fans as he evolved from an undrafted free agent to the Sixth Man of the Year in 2023-24. That made him a popular figure in Minneapolis.

It's tough to replicate that with basically any other team in the NBA, where he won't have that same kind of history.

Reid's adjustment to a new team could help explain his halftime benching in a 97-89 loss to the Detroit Pistons on Oct. 28. Coach Charles Lee said after the game he "didn't meet our standards in the first half."

Reid immediately assumed his usual role in the rotation, and he has performed particularly well of late. He had 25 points and 13 rebounds in a 124-112 victory over the Cleveland Cavaliers on Monday.

Reid is signed through the 2028-29 season and you'd assume he'll pick up his $28.4 million player option for 2029-30. The Hornets may like having that much team control when they haven't exactly been a magnet for free agents.

More likely is that Charlotte viewed the stretch big as a nice trade asset to flip to a contender from the moment he arrived in the LaMelo Ball trade.

articles.title: Robbie Avila Nears Contract for New Landing Spot in Latest Rumors After Lakers Stint, SLU Transfer
articles.summary: Former Saint Louis center Robbie Avila is "finalizing" a move to TCU and should arrive on the campus this week, according to ESPN's Pete Thamel.
articles.body:
Former Saint Louis center Robbie Avila is "finalizing" a move to TCU and should arrive on the campus this week, according to ESPN's Pete Thamel .

A judge granted Avila a preliminary injunction to play this season. After a four-year college career that began at Indiana State, he joined the Los Angeles Lakers as an undrafted free agent. He played for L.A. in the NBA Summer League but didn't sign a full pro contract.

A return to Saint Louis became complicated by the College Sports Commission declaring the Billikens couldn't have an extra spot to accommodate the 6'10" big man. As a result, he had to explore his options elsewhere.

Bryce James Stats vs. Northern Arizona 🔢

Avila was the Atlantic 10 Player of the Year in 2025-26, and he was a productive frontcourt presence for both Indiana State and Saint Louis. He's averaging 14.5 points, 5.5 rebounds and 0.6 blocks for his career.

TCU is already three games into its season, though. It can be difficult enough for an incoming transfer to find a comfort zone when they've had a full offseason to train and practice. Avila has to adapt totally on the fly.

The Horned Frogs can't make an addition of this caliber otherwise, so it's easy to see why they'd bring Avila to Fort Worth. They could use some size as well. They have six players averaging double figures in scoring, and none is taller than 6'9".

Fans may nonetheless want to temper expectations because there's a chance Avila is unable to have the kind of impact he did with his last two schools.

articles.title: Kevin Durant Reacts to Steph Curry's Injury, Hypes 'Problem' Yaxel Lendeborg After Win vs. Warriors
articles.summary: Kevin Durant sent well wishes to his former Golden State Warriors teammate after Stephen Curry left a Wednesday night matchup against the Houston Rockets with an apparent injury.
articles.body:
Kevin Durant sent well wishes to his former Golden State Warriors teammate after Stephen Curry left a Wednesday night matchup against the Houston Rockets with an apparent injury .

"Hopefully Steph's alright. He's been playing great ball. Their team's been playing great ball," Durant told ESPN's Jorge Sedano after the Rockets' 115-108 victory over the Warriors.

Head coach Steve Kerr said after the game the Warriors had a "high" level of concern while awaiting test results on Curry's right abdominal soreness.

Dray in Support of Yaxel's Trash Talk 🗣️

Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg led all players with 25 points while adding 10 rebounds in Curry's absence Wednesday night. He was also tasked with regularly defending Durant in what Kerr described as a "test" for the rookie.

Durant led the Rockets with 20 points on 8-for-17 shooting overall, but scored just three points while going 1-for-4 from the field when matched up against Lendeborg, per NBA.com .

When asked for his thoughts on Lendeborg, Durant told Sedano, "It's a problem, a matchup problem."

"Being that tall, and being that skilled, too— man, I'm excited to see his career unfold," Durant said.

Durant continued in his postgame press conference , saying: "Just love his game, to be honest. A skilled big that can play 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 on the offensive side of the ball. Can shoot it, can handle it, strong, long, athletic."

The Rockets star also cited Lendeborg's 7'3.25" wingspan as something that "right there just shows you he's a different level of athlete."

"He's been through a lot, man. So he came here fully full-grown, in my opinion, and he's ready for everything that's thrown at him," Durant said. "It was fun to play against him."

The Warriors were riding an eight-game win streak into Wednesday night's matchup against the Rockets.

Golden State will look to bounce back Friday at the San Antonio Spurs. Lendeborg, who is 12 games in to what has so far been one of the most efficient rookie seasons in NBA history, could be tasked with taking on an even more significant role in the matchup should Curry miss any time.

articles.title: TCU reportedly finalizing a deal to add Robbie Avila after he was blocked from playing for St. Louis
articles.summary: Robbie Avila was granted a fifth year of college eligibility in early November.
articles.body:
Former NCAA tournament star Robbie Avila will return to college basketball this season, just not with the team everyone expected. After being blocked from returning to St. Louis, Avila is reportedly finalizing a deal to join TCU, according to Field of 68's Jeff Goodman.

The report comes a week after Avila was granted a fifth year of college eligibility .

Avila, 23, was initially expected to return to St. Louis in his final year of eligibility, but ran into an issue with the College Sports Commission (CSC), which ruled that St. Louis already had 15 players on its roster and could not add Avila as its 16th player. The CSC issued that ruling despite St. Louis City Circuit Court Judge Jason Sengheiser ruling that the team could roster Avila as a 16th player.

In its statement, the CSC noted that Avila "may be eligible to play college basketball this season," but not for a team that doesn't have the roster space.

Avila was among the many athletes from the high school class of 2022 to fight for a fifth year of college eligibility. After playing out his senior season at St. Louis, Avila went undrafted in the 2026 NBA Draft. He then agreed to an Exhibition 10 contract with the Los Angeles Lakers and played in the Summer League. Avila later argued that he never signed a deal, only verbally agreed to one. That gambit worked, and Avila was granted eligibility to return to college.

Whether Avila actually suits up for TCU remains to be seen. A number of athletes have tried to return to college after receiving experience in the pros. While some — Charles Bediako — were able to return, they did so temporarily before eventually being deemed ineligible.

LSU's football team found itself in a similar spot with former Ole Miss players Dae'Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris. Both players were granted another year of college eligibility, but were eventually left off LSU's roster after the SEC threatened the school. It's unclear whether the Big 12 or its teams would put up a similar fight against Avila.

If he's allowed to suit up, Avila could be a significant addition to TCU. After averaging 12.8 points, 4.5 rebounds and 4.1 assists per game last season, Avila earned Atlantic 10 Player of the Year honors with St. Louis.

articles.title: Gabe Vincent's 'Standing' Contract Offer Revealed in New NBA Rumors Following Knicks Interest
articles.summary: Veteran guard Gabe Vincent has a "standing offer" from the Sacramento Kings, according The Stein Line's Mark Stein.
articles.body:
Veteran guard Gabe Vincent has a "standing offer" from the Sacramento Kings, according The Stein Line's Mark Stein .

Stein previously reported in September the New York Knicks showed interest in Vincent, but he "elected to wait for a more sure-fire opportunity."

The Atlanta Hawks acquired Vincent from the Los Angeles Lakers midway through the 2025-26 season, with Luke Kennard heading to Los Angeles. In 53 games between the two teams, he averaged 4.4 points and 1.4 assists in 16.6 minutes on the floor.

The 30-year-old was another Miami Heat player development success story by the time he last hit free agency in 2023. Starting his career in the NBA G League, he emerged as a valuable role player for Miami.

Vincent's performance in the 2023 playoffs couldn't have lined up better. He shot 37.8 percent from beyond the arc and averaged 12.7 points as Miami reached the NBA Finals.

The Lakers signed Vincent to a three-year, $33 million contract that summer. The move proved to be a costly mistake for L.A.

Injuries limited Vincent to 11 games in his first year in purple and gold, and he was generally unable to recapture the peak he enjoyed in South Florida. During the Lakers' back-to-back first-round playoff exits, he scored 21 total points and went 5-of-20 from long range.

Perhaps as a result of the knee trouble from early in his Los Angeles tenure, Vincent has become almost exclusively a three-point shooter. He maintained a 62.9 percent three-point rate in Miami, and that number climbed to 75.8 percent over the past two years, per Basketball Reference .

That's not ideal for a player who has a sub-34 percent career clip from deep.

Vincent historically hasn't been much of a playmaker, either. According to Basketball Reference, he's dishing out 3.5 assists per 36 minutes through his seven seasons.

The Kings would at the very least give Vincent a showcase. He'd be an option off the bench behind starting guards Darius Acuff Jr. and Zach LaVine.

When Sacramento is 1-10 to open the season, it's easy to see why he's still waiting to see if a different opportunity presents itself.

articles.title: Stephen Curry Injury Update, Latest News and Timeline to Return for Warriors Star
articles.summary: Golden State Warriors star Stephen Curry will miss at least two weeks with an oblique abdominal tear, the team announced Thursday:
articles.body:
Golden State Warriors star Stephen Curry will miss at least two weeks with an oblique abdominal tear, the team announced Thursday:

Curry exited Wednesday's loss against the Houston Rockets in the first quarter and was holding his right side as he went to the locker room. He was ruled out for the remainder of the contest due to right abdominal soreness.

Warriors head coach Steve Kerr said that Curry left the game to have an MRI done.

"At halftime, prior to leaving for the MRI, Curry spoke to his teammates and told them to focus on the task at hand, assuring them that he would get through this latest injury fine," ESPN's Anthony Slater reported.

The injury comes amid an 8-4 start to the season for the Warriors. Curry is putting up 27.8 points, 3.9 assists and 3.7 rebounds per game so far.

Curry, 38, had back-to-back seasons with 70-plus games played, but he managed to play in just 43 games last season because of a lingering knee issue. In his 17th NBA season, Curry put up 26.6 points, 4.7 assists and 3.6 rebounds per game as the Warriors missed the playoffs.

He hoped to come into his 18th season fully healthy, but he suffered a right ankle sprain in practice on Oct. 18, less than a week before the Warriors began the 2026-27 campaign. Luckily, he was ready to go for the start of the season.

He's missed two of the Warriors' first 11 games, though it was only for the purpose of getting him rest amid back-to-back games.

Unfortunately for Golden State, injuries have been the story over the last few years. Along with Curry missing almost half of the 2025-26 campaign, Jimmy Butler played just 38 games before suffering a season-ending torn ACL in January.

When healthy, the Warriors have the talent to make a playoff run, but given the aging stars on their roster, avoiding injuries might be an issue again this year.

articles.title: Warriors' Stephen Curry out at least 2 weeks after suffering oblique abdominal tear
articles.summary: Curry exited Wednesday's loss to the Rockets in the first quarter.
articles.body:
Stephen Curry will miss at least the next two weeks after suffering an oblique abdominal tear, the Golden State Warriors announced Thursday .

Curry suffered the injury in the opening quarter of Wednesday's 115-108 loss to the Houston Rockets . He was spotted reaching for his side after drilling a 3-pointer in the opening minutes, and he seemed frustrated about it, but he wasn't touched and remained in the game at the time.

He would later leave the floor during a timeout to go directly into the Warriors' dressing room with a trainer.

Curry stayed in the locker room for the rest of the opening quarter. The team then ruled him out at the start of the second quarter with what they called right abdominal soreness.

After exiting the game, Curry underwent an MRI, which confirmed the tear. The Warriors said the point guard will be re-evaluated in two weeks.

Head coach Steve Kerr said Curry had tweaked something in the abdominal area that he "had never done" before.

Curry finished the night with three points and a turnover in the six minutes he was on the floor. The 38-year-old entered the night averaging 30.6 points, 4.3 assists and 4.1 rebounds per game this season, his 18th in the league.

articles.title: SGA Hypes Drake as GOAT Rapper, Thunder Star Ranks Favorite Albums in Spotify Interview
articles.summary: The Toronto ties appear to be strong between Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and Drake, as the two-time NBA MVP believes OVO stands at the top of the all-time rapper list.
articles.body:
The Toronto ties appear to be strong between Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and Drake, as the two-time NBA MVP believes OVO stands at the top of the all-time rapper list.

In an interview with Spotify (starts at 1:40 mark), Gilgeous-Alexander revealed he considers Drake to be the greatest rapper of all-time while also declaring Take Care and Nothing Was the Same to be his best albums.

The Oklahoma City Thunder star ranked Take Care and Nothing Was the Same as 1A and 1B in Drake's discography, followed by Iceman "right underneath" and also the best album of 2026.

Gilgeous-Alexander previously had Iceman list as his favorite Drake album ahead of Take Care in a blind ranking video posted by the Thunder in September, though he did acknowledge in the Spotify interview he "might have messed" up the order after discussing it with his friends.

There was no indication of any bias on Gilgeous-Alexander's part when he deemed Drake to be the greatest rapper of all-time, though one could suggest it exists since both are famously from Toronto.

Drake is far more connected to The Six at this point since he regularly attends Raptors games. Gilgeous-Alexander has spent the bulk of his NBA career in Oklahoma City, but he did represent his home country at the 2024 Olympics.

Canada's appearance at the Paris Games was its first time in the Olympics since 2000. Gilgeous-Alexander led Team Canada to a fifth-place finish.

articles.title: Warriors' Charles Bassey Rips Marcus Smart's 'Fake Toughness' After Getting Punched on Video
articles.summary: Golden State Warriors center Charles Bassey commented Wednesday night after Houston Rockets guard Marcus Smart got ejected for throwing a punch at him during Houston's 115-108 home win.
articles.body:
Golden State Warriors center Charles Bassey commented Wednesday night after Houston Rockets guard Marcus Smart got ejected for throwing a punch at him during Houston's 115-108 home win.

Speaking to reporters following the game, Bassey called out Smart's "fake toughness," before adding, "I don't think he was trying to play. I think he was trying to get himself out of the game."

Late in the third quarter, Smart and Bassey exchanged words, prompting Smart to throw a punch toward Bassey's face:

Smart was assessed a flagrant foul 2, resulting in his immediate ejection from the game.

Bassey noted that he expected Smart to do something because Smart had been "playing dirty the whole game."

Houston ended Golden State's eight-game winning streak with the victory, dropping the Warriors to 8-4 on the season, while the Rockets improved to 9-3.

Prior to his ejection, Smart recorded six points, two rebounds and one assist in 17 minutes off the bench.

Meanwhile, Bassey played 13 minutes off the bench, finishing with seven points, six rebounds and one block.

The Rockets led by eight points at the time of Smart's ejection, but it did little to swing the momentum in Golden State's favor.

Undoubtedly the biggest concern coming out of the game for Golden State was the health of superstar guard Stephen Curry, who left in the fourth quarter and was diagnosed Thursday with an oblique abdominal tear that will keep him out for at least two weeks.

As for the budding rivalry between the Warriors and Rockets, it won't be renewed until Dec. 30 when Golden State hosts Houston.

articles.title: Malik Beasley spends night on TikTok Live selling game-worn, autographed jerseys amid gambling scandal
articles.summary: The former Detroit Pistons guard Malik Beasley has turned to an unexpected source of income, spending hours on TikTok Live selling autographed jerseys from h...
articles.body:
The former Detroit Pistons guard Malik Beasley has turned to an unexpected source of income, spending hours on TikTok Live selling autographed jerseys from his NBA career. His livestream quickly caught the attention of basketball fans, especially as his future in the league remains uncertain amid an ongoing federal gambling investigation.

Clips shared by TheDunkCentral and MrBuckBuckNBA showed Beasley displaying memorabilia and promoting sales during the livestream. He also reassured viewers about the jerseys' authenticity. When asked about a Minnesota Timberwolves jersey, he responded, "Ooh, I do have a T-Wolves jersey, but it's for a boy. I need it. I need it." Another clip showed him continuing the stream despite appearing exhausted .

The livestream comes as Beasley faces serious uncertainty following a federal investigation into an alleged gambling scheme. According to The Athletic , the guard has agreed to plead guilty , with a formal hearing scheduled for December 9, 2026, in Brooklyn. The case concerns alleged manipulation of player performance for betting purposes during his time with the Milwaukee Bucks in the 2023-24 season.

The investigation also disrupted what could have been a major payday. Beasley was reportedly in line for a three-year, $42 million contract with Detroit after finishing second in Sixth Man of the Year voting in 2025. The deal never materialized following the emergence of the gambling allegations.

Beasley previously earned nearly $60 million in NBA salary over nine seasons. His recent livestream has therefore sparked reactions about his financial situation and uncertain playing future.

While fans debated the jersey sales, Malik Beasley's upcoming court appearance could prove far more consequential. His expected guilty plea may also put his NBA career at further risk.

articles.title: Canucks Rundown: Sedins Address Media, Thursday Practice
articles.summary: Thursday’s Canucks Rundown will cover notes from Henrik and Daniel Sedin’s media availability and the day’s practice. Sedins Address Media […]
articles.body:
Thursday's Canucks Rundown will cover notes from Henrik and Daniel Sedin's media availability and the day's practice.

The Sedins opened up their availability by saying that it reflected a commitment to transparency. Compared to the previous regime, the new management group has been more open to answering questions, either in media availabilities or on local sports shows. "We took this job because we were tired of being mediocre," Henrik Sedin said about rebuilding.

"We are certainly not happy with our results, and nobody should be," commented Daniel Sedin, as reporters asked about the start of the season. Henrik Sedin also discussed the team's execution and had no criticism of the systems in place. "It's easy to look at the system when you're losing…but within the structure, you need to execute," he said. He also stated that he knows the roster is better than the start indicates, and that everyone knows it.

Demko, Young Players, Trades, and Avoiding the Retool

On the status of Thatcher Demko, Henrik Sedin answered, "He's here, he's rehabbing, he's in a good mood, and he's getting better." In addition, he said that there is no real timeline. Previously, an estimate of a return around Christmas was given, but now, it appears that Demko will not be rushed back, which makes sense. Lankinen and Meriläinen will need to hold down the fort for a while longer.

It is definitely not easy for young players to enter the NHL on a rebuilding squad. Errors are more costly, and adversity feels like it is striking every day. Henrik commented that in the modern NHL, it is common for young players to enter the league on rebuilding teams. It is how they handle the adversity that is really telling about who they are. Indeed, a lot of the teams on the rise, such as the San Jose Sharks, Anaheim Ducks, and Montreal Canadiens, have had their star players get acquainted with the NHL in the midst of rebuilds.

The Vancouver Canucks still have to have veterans to support their young players. Henrik emphasized that they cannot simply trade all of their veterans for draft picks, and they look to improve the team every day. "We're not going to trade away players just to get more draft picks," said Henrik. "You also need to put a better product on the ice." Daniel also added that draft picks alone would not get them through a rebuild.

At the same time, they are committed to rebuilding the right way. Both Sedins talked about how they could have opted for a retool and sold the fans on it, but the goal is not simply to make the Stanley Cup Playoffs, but to do it consistently. Short-term pain is needed for long-term gain.

You can check out the full press conference from the Sedins via Sportsnet's website.

articles.title: Dame Time is back in Portland — and the Blazers look dangerous
articles.summary: A new Blazers season brings a new starting lineup, a new coach, a new ownership group and a new set of expectations.
articles.body:
A new head coach will roam the sidelines. A franchise icon will make his long-awaited return. An All-Star will begin his redemption tour.

And a new ownership group will watch its first season opener from Paul Allen's former seats along the Moda Center baseline.

The Blazers open the 2026-27 NBA season Wednesday night against the Phoenix Suns — a team they upset in April in the play-in tournament — and if you're just now tuning in for the start of the regular season, well, there's a lot you missed.

What does the starting lineup look like?

The Blazers are expected to unveil a new starting lineup that features a pair of notable All-Star additions: Damian Lillard and Ja Morant . The backcourt duo is joining a fivesome that includes returning starters Deni Avdija , Toumani Camara and Donovan Clingan . It's a versatile, star-studded lineup that features three All-Stars, a former All-Defensive Second Team selection, one of the best young centers in the NBA and loads of scoring potential.

Micah Nori , the Blazers' first-year head coach, said he plans on using a 10-man rotation to start the season, which will allow the Blazers to capitalize on their depth and versatility. In addition to the starters, Jrue Holiday, Scoot Henderson, Sidy Cissoko, Robert Williams III and Vit Krejci are expected to open the season in the rotation. The group could change depending on matchups and Williams' availability — he did not play in back-to-backs last season — and it's likely that Micah Potter, Branden Carlson and Yang Hansen will occasionally see spot duty, as well.

The Blazers stabilized their turbulent coaching situation in June, hiring longtime NBA assistant Nori to replace interim coach Tiago Splitter . Nori, who interviewed for head coaching jobs seven times before finally landing his first chance, is entering his 29th season in the league and is universally revered in NBA circles for his positive approach, ability to connect with players and sharp basketball mind. Early indications have been encouraging, as the Blazers players seem to love him and the front office works well with him. The Blazers' coaching position had been embroiled in controversy, of course, as former coach Chauncey Billups — who was placed on indefinite leave by the NBA — is facing federal felony charges related to money laundering and wire fraud conspiracy for his alleged involvement in a rigged underground poker game.

In a stark contrast to recent seasons, the Blazers are constructed around their offense rather than their defense. The roster is unbalanced, featuring five dynamic ball-handlers and playmakers (Lillard, Morant, Avdija, Holiday and Henderson), a solid center combination (Clingan and Williams) and little wing depth. As a result, the team is expected to play fast and free under Nori, bringing lots of speed, passing, cutting and flow. Nori said he hopes to rotate his players liberally in shorter shifts during games — perhaps as short as three minutes — which will enable them to play with maximum effort before giving way to teammates. The interior defense is strong with Clingan and Williams patrolling the middle, Camara remains one of the NBA's best and most versatile defenders and Cissoko will be asked to guard one-through-five. Holiday is still capable of locking down opposing guards and Avdija has pledged to be more of a two-way threat now that he doesn't have to serve as the team's primary ball-handler. But the backcourt combination of Morant and Lillard, while lethal on offense, is not imposing on defense and relatively small (both stand 6-foot-2).

Portland defied pundits last season, winning 10 of its last 14 regular season games to secure a spot in the play-in tournament, where it beat the Suns in Phoenix to earn the seventh seed in the Western Conference. The San Antonio Spurs dismissed the Blazers with a gentleman's sweep in the playoffs , but the strong run — combined with the additions of Lillard and Morant — has raised expectations in Portland. How much? Camara said in training camp that the Blazers' goal is to win 50 or more games and secure home-court advantage in the postseason. It won't be easy. The league is as deep and talented as ever, and new rules surrounding the lottery should discourage teams from tanking, meaning most of the league will be chasing wins instead of lottery ping-pong balls late into the season. It seemed like a third of the league had given up last year by the All-Star break.

As the Blazers' new-look lineup works to build chemistry and a first-year coach settles into a new role, the schedule will be challenging. Six of the first eight games — and 12 of the first 17 — will come on the road and include a slew of playoff contenders, including the Spurs, Oklahoma City Thunder (twice), Minnesota Timberwolves (twice), New York Knicks, Philadelphia 76ers, Denver Nuggets and Los Angeles Lakers (twice).

The most uplifting part of opening night figures to be the return of Lillard, the franchise icon who is back after spending two seasons in Milwaukee and one season on the injured list. The nine-time All-Star and franchise leader has not played in an NBA regular-season or playoff game since April 27, 2025, when he suffered a torn left Achilles tendon. And he has not played with Portland since March 22, 2023, six months before it traded him to the Bucks. Lillard showed no ill effects from his injury during the exhibition season, when he played in three of the Blazers' four games and averaged 17.3 points, 2.7 assists and 22.7 minutes. If anything, he looked like the same old Dame, swishing three-pointers, creating off the dribble, initiating offense and drawing defensive attention. Lillard joked earlier this week that he's "not an old man," but also acknowledged that he isn't likely to play upward of 38 minutes a game like he used to and may even take a night off here and there for rest, most likely on a random back-to-back. His addition not only should help cover up two of the Blazers' biggest weaknesses last season — three-point shooting and shooting in the clutch — but also inspire a thirsty fan base, which has rarely loved a player more. All the while, Lillard says he intends to play with more "joy" than ever.

articles.title: New NBA Rumors on Darius Acuff Jr.'s Impact on Potential Kings Coaching Change
articles.summary: The development of rookie guard Darius Acuff Jr. is a consideration for the Sacramento Kings as they evaluate their coaching situation, according to The Athletic's Sam Amick.
articles.body:
The development of rookie guard Darius Acuff Jr. is a consideration for the Sacramento Kings as they evaluate their coaching situation, according to The Athletic's Sam Amick.

Amick reported on Sactown Sports 1140 the Kings would prefer to stick with Doug Christie for the duration of the 2026-27 NBA season. He added they "don't want" Acuff to have multiple head coaches in just one year if they can avoid it:

Sacramento is 1-10, so it's almost certainly heading toward a fourth straight season of missing the playoffs. More importantly, Christie might be coaching to save his job rather than doing what's best for the organization's long-term outlook.

Amick reported Wednesday the Kings felt compelled to trade 2025 first-round pick Nique Clifford because he was getting so little playing time. In two games with the Oklahoma City Thunder, Clifford's usage (36 minutes) is already approaching how much he played in eight appearances with Sacramento (50 minutes).

That's not a specific concern with Acuff, who's the starting point guard and leading the team in scoring at 26.2 points. Keeping a lame-duck coach who's either auditioning for his current employer or a new team does, however, raise the risk of a young player developing some bad habits on the court.

Christie is also pushing Acuff pretty hard, perhaps because his priorities are a little misdirected.

For the reasons Amick alluded to, the alternative isn't a lot better.

With so much time left in the season, the Kings probably wouldn't have an interim finish out the year after firing Christie. They'd hire a full-time replacement eventually, giving them three different sideline leaders in one year.

Even if everyone assumes Christie is a goner and the losses continue to pile up, maintaining some continuity may be the best route forward if Acuff's growth is a major focus for the front office.

articles.title: James Harden Calls Out Critics, Says 'People Are Going to Talk' After Cavs' Win vs. Knicks
articles.summary: James Harden shrugged off criticism regarding his slow start to the 2026-27 campaign after scoring a season-high 32 points in Wednesday night's win over the New York Knicks.
articles.body:
James Harden shrugged off criticism regarding his slow start to the 2026-27 campaign after scoring a season-high 32 points in Wednesday night's win over the New York Knicks.

"I was averaging 36 and 35, whatever the case may be, people had something to say about that. 'You can't win like that.' So then I averaged 20-something, it's like, 'can't win like that,'" Harden said after winning in Madison Square Garden, per Brian Mahoney of the Associated Press.

"So I think the most important thing for me, like, people are going to talk. So I just focus on myself, things I need to do and try to get in really good shape and learn my teammates and learn how to play a different brand of basketball, because I'm not the same fast person that I was like five or six years ago."

Harden's Surprising Admission About Fitness 🤔

Harden put up his Wednesday night scoring total on 9-for-14 shooting from the field, including 5-for-7 from deep, to go along with nine made shots on 11 attempts from the free-throw line.

Both Harden and Donovan Mitchell expressed confidence after the game that Harden would continue bouncing back after a sluggish start:

"It's my 18th year. My name is James Harden. I used to score a lot of points," Harden said (h/t KOS magazin's Darko Dželetović). "Now it's like... I still score points, but I find other ways to impact the game as well, and I think that's what people don't understand.

"Donovan averages a lot of points. He's a scoring machine on this team. So, just picking and choosing when I have opportunities to be aggressive and score, and then do other things to impact wins. Get off to a slow start, but I think I'll find out my rhythm... eventually things will turn around."

Mitchell said in an appearance on ESPN's SportsCenter Harden's success "alleviates a lot of pressure" from the rest of the Cavaliers roster.

"I think tonight, he's starting to find it in different ways," Mitchell said. "I think the biggest thing now is just continuing to play that way, continuing to do those things. We have all the trust in him, and tonight was a great example of that."

Mitchell and the Cavaliers will now hope to see Harden ride the momentum of his most productive outing of the season into a Friday night road game against the Miami Heat. The Heat, after a slow season start of their own, are heading into the matchup on a 5-2 streak.

articles.title: Heat Linked to 2 Vets as Potential Signings in New NBA Rumors amid Slow Start to Season
articles.summary: The Miami Heat are reportedly considering signing reuniting Kevin Porter Jr. and Giannis Antetokounmpo.
articles.body:
The Miami Heat are reportedly considering signing reuniting Kevin Porter Jr. and Giannis Antetokounmpo.

The Heat have "weighed signing a free agent like Kevin Porter Jr. or Heat alumnus Gabe Vincent to try to manufacture some immediate help" after a 5-6 start to the season, NBA insider Jake Fischer reported for The Stein Line's Substack.

Porter, who spent parts of two seasons playing with Antetokounmpo and the Milwaukee Bucks, has been a free agent since he was waived by Milwaukee in October.

He averaged 17.4 points and a career-high 7.4 assists for the Bucks when available last season, but missed most of the campaign with a right knee injury.

Marc Stein and Fischer previously connected the Sacramento Kings to an interest in Porter following Ben Simmons' season-ending Achilles injury. The Portland Trail Blazers and Denver Nuggets have also shown interest in Porter, per Fischer .

Vincent went unsigned this offseason after averaging 4.4 and 1.4 assists last season in a campaign split between the Los Angeles Lakers and Atlanta Hawks.

Stein previously reported Vincent has drawn interest from the New York Knicks and has a " standing offer " from the Sacramento Kings.

The Heat struggled as Bam Adebayo worked to find his fit with Antetokounmpo during an 0-4 start to the season.

Miami has turned things around by winning three of its last four games, although those victories came against opponents that have combined for a total of four wins so far this season in the Los Angeles Clippers, Utah Jazz and Kings.

The Heat have a tougher schedule ahead, starting over the next week with games against the Cleveland Cavaliers, Detroit Pistons and Houston Rockets. How the team performs over this stretch could influence what answers the Heat seeks in free agency.

Should Miami later look for help via trade rather than adding through free agency, Fischer speculated some moves could take place sooner rather than later.

According to Fischer, a "cap strategist contacted by The Stein Line suggested that we could see teams with losing records try to make their first trade moves" around Dec. 15 rather than the February deadline because that's when players on contracts signed last offseason are eligible to be traded.

articles.title: James Harden Makes Surprising Admission About Fitness Amid Cavs' Slow Start to 2026 NBA Season
articles.summary: James Harden had a pretty slow start to the 2026-27 season before Wednesday night's 32 points in a 115-107 win over the New York Knicks.
articles.body:
James Harden had a pretty slow start to the 2026-27 season before Wednesday night's 32 points in a 115-107 win over the New York Knicks.

One of the reasons? Harden didn't play much basketball over the summer and acknowledged he came into training camp relatively out of shape.

"I knew it was going to take a little bit of time to get adjusted to the speed, the pace, all of the above," he told reporters after the Knicks' win. "I'm not young, so I can't just be ready (immediately), so I already knew that coming into the season. So now it's like, all right, cool, (now) I feel really good. And the work is automatically getting put in. That's why I have been able to last so long in this league."

He added that he's "trying to get in really good shape and learn my teammates."

Whether the 37-year-old Harden was trying to carefully manage the workload on his body or just decided on an elongated vacation over the summer is unclear, but it has resulted in rough start to the 2026-27 season.

If Wednesday night is closer to the norm going forward, however, the Cavs will be in far better shape going forward. All because Harden, apparently, has been playing his way into shape to start the season.

articles.title: New NBA Rumors on Trade Market for Pacers, Kings, Nets, More Struggling Teams
articles.summary: Through the early stages of the 2026-27 NBA campaign, top teams have started to reveal themselves while teams destined to miss the playoffs are also starting to become clear.
articles.body:
Through the early stages of the 2026-27 NBA campaign, top teams have started to reveal themselves while teams destined to miss the playoffs are also starting to become clear.

But unlike most years, bottom feeders won't benefit from an all-out tank.

Under the new 3-2-1 lottery system , the bottom three teams will have just a 5.4 percent chance of earning the top pick in the draft. NBA insider Jake Fischer reported that, because of the new system, one Eastern Conference team strategist said, "there will be less sellers than ever before" at the trade deadline.

Fischer pointed to the Sacramento Kings as an example. The Kings are 1-10 and are long shots at making the playoffs, but because they need to finish better than the bottom three in the league, they "need to add talent immediately rather than subtract."

"Will everybody be buyers at the trade deadline?" one Western Conference executive asked Fischer.

Fischer also noted that the Indiana Pacers, who are 4-8 amid a Tyrese Haliburton injury, "have indeed begun sniffing around at potential mid-tier improvements."

The Brooklyn Nets don't control their own pick in the first round of the 2027 draft, so avoiding a bottom-three record isn't paramount. Instead, Fischer pointed out that they could "populate the market with some trade candidates," as could the Milwaukee Bucks and Los Angeles Clippers.

The Miami Heat, who are off to a 5-6 start despite the addition of Giannis Antetokounmpo, have eyed free agents like Kevin Porter Jr. and Gabe Vincent, according to Fischer.

articles.title: Caleb Wilson Injured, Latest Rumors on Bulls Star's Return Timeline After Suffering Hand Fracture
articles.summary: A dismal season reportedly took another bad turn for the Chicago Bulls.
articles.body:
A dismal season reportedly took another bad turn for the Chicago Bulls.

ESPN's Shams Charania reported Thursday that promising rookie Caleb Wilson suffered a fractured right hand and needs surgery. He is expected to miss four to six weeks for the 1-9 Bulls.

Wilson suffered the injury during Wednesday's loss to the San Antonio Spurs.

He was excellent prior to the setback with 15 points and five rebounds in 15 minutes of action as he went up against a frontcourt led by Victor Wembanyama.

The No. 4 pick in the 2026 NBA draft has been a significant bright spot for a Bulls team that doesn't have many others. He is averaging 18.9 points, 6.2 rebounds and 1.8 steals per game while shooting 42 percent from the field in his rookie campaign.

Wilson looks like a foundational cornerstone for the Bulls, and his long-term health is more important than the immediate future of what is already shaping up to be a lost season. Chicago will surely take a cautious approach when it comes to clearing him to return even with an expected timeframe of a month or more.

Head coach Tiago Splitter even suggested the team needs a "smart" approach with the North Carolina product.

"We've got to be smart with him of course," he told reporters . "He's playing a lot of minutes. Those minutes are important to his development, but we've also got to be smart with his body being young. I think there's a false thought that when you're young you can do whatever but that's not true. You've got to get stronger, you've got to get your body prepared to face a season like the NBA, so we've got to be careful there and we've got to monitor it for sure."

The Bulls could give more minutes to Leonard Miller or Noa Essengue in the meantime, but Wilson's health will be the most important development for the coming weeks.

articles.title: TJ Shots lleva al Valencia a su mejor arranque histórico en la Euroliga
articles.standfirst: Con 14 puntos y 10 asistencias lidera a su equipo ante el Bayern Múnich
articles.summary: Con 14 puntos y 10 asistencias lidera a su equipo ante el Bayern Múnich
articles.body: El Valencia Basket sometió este jueves al Bayern Munich (102-87) en un encuentro en el que dominó de principio a fin al conjunto alemán con una buena defensa de primera línea y otra gran actuación de TJ Shorts, que sumó 14 puntos y repartió 10 asistencias. El triunfo permite al conjunto de Xavi Albert mantenerse en la zona alta de la clasificación y su balance de 8-3 tras los once primeros encuentros en la competición supone su mejor arranque histórico en la Euroliga. El Valencia Basket dominó ya con solvencia el inicio. La defensa de Mario Saint-Supéry colapsó a Rokas Jokubaitis y de rebote el juego colectivo alemán y en ataque, al ritmo de TJ Shorts, los locales se hicieron con la iniciativa del marcador (10-2, m.4). No tardó en pararlo Anton Gavel que, al menos, consiguió que su equipo empezara a anotar con Washington a los mandos y Wiley barriendo los rebotes en el aro local. Pero también el Valencia supo encontrar a un confiado Neal Sako en la otra zona y los equilibrios se mantuvieron (26-17, m.9). El Bayern consiguió ser más incisivo y sacar faltas a la defensa 'taronja', lo que le dio puntos desde el tiro libre y cortó ritmo a los locales. Pero el Valencia no se puso nervioso, en parte porque un par de triples de Gonzalo Corbalán y de Armori Brooks alimentaron su casillero y compensaron el despertar de Andy Obst. El conjunto alemán vio cómo Óscar Da Silva, uno de sus jugadores más sólidos, se tuvo que ir al banquillo con tres faltas pero de nuevo la dupla que formaron Obst y Wiley le permitió llegar vivo al descanso (52-41, m.20). Regresó mejor de nuevo el Valencia pero le faltó colmillo y constancia para abrir hueco y el Bayern, con una mejor circulación de balón y de nuevo con Da Silva de estilete, logró reducir su desventaja y amenazar el dominio del encuentro. La labor de intendencia de Jasiel Rivero y de Josep Puerto, pese a su mal porcentaje de triples, permitió al Valencia superar ese bache y dio tiempo a que TJ Shorts retomara el mando del encuentro y recuperara parte de la renta perdida por los suyos (80-67, m.32). Un par de triples locales, uno del hiperactivo Cárdenas y otro de Osetkowski, y un par de buenas permitieron al Valencia abrir brecha y romper definitivamente el choque pese a que Obst no dejó de anotar desde la línea de 6,75, aunque no bastó para complicarle el final al sólido equipo de Xavi Albert. 102 - Valencia Basket (29+23+21+29): TJ Shorts (14), Saint-Supéry (6), Taylor (7), Osetkowski (9), Sako (11) -cinco titular- Cárdenas (9), Moore (-), Corbalán (10), Brooks (14), Puerto (10), Gueye (2) y Rivero (10). 87 - Bayern Múnich (19+22+24+22): Jokubaitis (10), Obst (22), Lucic (4), Da Silva (12), Thiemann (6) -cinco titular- Norris (4), Beauchamp (4), Washington (13), Voigtmann (-), Wiley (10) y Jessup (2). articles.title: NBA suspends Rockets G Marcus Smart 3 games for throwing punch at Warriors' Charles Bassey
articles.summary: Throwing punches is an automatic suspension in the NBA.
articles.body:
The NBA doesn't look kindly on players who throw punches during a game. Houston Rockets guard Marcus Smart was suspended three games without pay by the NBA on Thursday after throwing a punch at Golden State Warriors center Charles Bassey during Wednesday's game.

In its statement , the league specifically says the punch made contact with Bassey's face. The suspension is set to cover Houston's games against the Utah Jazz on Friday, the Washington Wizards on Sunday and the Miami Heat on Monday.

The incident occurred in the third quarter of Houston's 115-108 win . With less than a minute to go in the quarter, Smart and Bassey appeared to exchange words on the court. Smart then threw a punch at Bassey right in front of an official.

Smart was assessed with a flagrant 2 foul and ejected from the contest. He had already exited the court by the time the officials announced the punishment.

Smart finished the game with 6 points, 2 rebounds and 1 assist.

Under NBA rules, Smart faced — at the minimum — a fine for the flagrant foul and a suspension for throwing a punch, which comes with a minimum one-game ban in the NBA rulebook :

Any player who throws a punch, whether it connects or not, has committed an unsportsmanlike act. He will be ejected following confirmation during review by instant replay and suspended for a minimum of one game.

The incident occurred after Smart and Bassey got tangled up during a rebound attempt. Following the contest, Rockets coach Ime Udoka said Smart confronted Bassey after the Warriors center wrapped up Smart's elbow on the play. Bassey reportedly told Smart "what are you gonna do," leading to the attempted punch.

Bassey, meanwhile, had something to say about what he called "fake toughness" from Smart:

"He's been playing dirty the whole game," Bassey said, according to Yahoo Sports' Kelly Iko . "I don't think he was trying to play, I think he was trying to get kicked out of the game."

Smart's absence didn't hurt the Rockets too badly in the end, as the team still managed to pull off a win. It probably helped that Warriors star Stephen Curry sustained an oblique tear early in the contest , missing much of the game.

articles.title: Marcus Smart's Punishment for Punching Charles Bassey Announced By NBA After Rockets vs. Warriors
articles.summary: The NBA suspended Houston Rockets guard Marcus Smart for three games after he punched Golden State Warriors center Charles Bassey during a matchup between the two teams on Wednesday, via NBA insider Chris Haynes.
articles.body:
The NBA suspended Houston Rockets guard Marcus Smart for three games after he punched Golden State Warriors center Charles Bassey during a matchup between the two teams on Wednesday, via NBA insider Chris Haynes.

In the third quarter of Houston's 115-108 win over Golden State, Smart threw a punch at Bassey before they were separated by their teammates. Smart was given a flagrant 2 foul for the incident and ejected from the game.

Bassey weighed in on the situation after the contest.

"He's been playing dirty the whole game, man," Bassey said, per Dalton Johnson of NBC Sports Bay Area. "I remember in the first half, I was trying to set a screen. Bro, he grabbed my knees. He was playing dirty."

"I don't think he was trying to play," he added. "I think he was trying to get himself out of the game. He wasn't trying to play, because if he was trying to play, you don't do that bro. I think he was trying to chill. He wasn't trying to hoop, bro. Like I said, man, that was fake. Fake toughness."

Rockets head coach Ime Udoka detailed Smart's perspective as well.

"Refs didn't say anything. I didn't see it but I just talked to Marcus," Udoka told reporters, via SI.com's Eric Jay Santos . "He said they got wrapped up, and his elbow that he had hurt got bent up. So he said something to him, and Bassey said, 'What you going to do?' And he did it."

Smart's three-game suspension will cost him $125,462, while the Rockets are set to receive a tax variance credit or $62,731 (h/t ESPN's Bobby Marks ).

The veteran guard has been known for his aggressive perimeter defense throughout his career, earning three All-Defensive Team selections to go with a Defensive Player of the Year award in 2022.

Smart previously received a one-game suspension for language directed at an official in 2021. He was also suspended one game for striking former San Antonio Spurs center Matt Bonner in the groin in 2015.

This season, Smart is averaging 8.3 points, 2.6 rebounds and 2.0 assists per game while shooting 43.9 percent from the field and 40.0 percent from behind the arc.

Meanwhile, Bassey is in the midst of his first full year on the Warriors after suiting up for four teams during his 2025-26 campaign. He's appeared in 10 games this season, recording 7.6 points and 5.7 rebounds on a nightly basis while connecting on 66.7 percent of his field goals.

Smart will be eligible to return from his latest suspension against the Indiana Pacers on Nov. 18.

articles.title: LeBron James sitting out 76ers' matchup vs. Raptors  due to back management; Joel Embiid available after being questionable to play
articles.summary: Both James and Embiid have missed two of the 76ers' 12 games this season.
articles.body:
LeBron James will sit out his third game of the early 2026-27 season for the Philadelphia 76ers' matchup with the Toronto Raptors on Thursday.

James is listed on the Sixers' injury report as out with "low back/sciatica management," which has been the reason he's sat two of Philadelphia's previous 12 games this season.

The 41-year-old was listed as questionable until participating in Thursday's shootaround. He was then downgraded.

Joel Embiid is available in what appeared to be a game-time decision. He was listed on the injury report as questionable with "right foot plantar fascia injury management," which has also sidelined him for two of the Sixers' game in the early season. However, his status was upgraded at 6:30 p.m. ET, a half-hour before tip-off.

"I have no idea," Embiid said when asked by ESPN's Kris Rhim if he was playing versus the Raptors. "We'll see what they have to say and then we'll go from there."

Thursday's game is not part of a back-to-back for the 76ers, so that is not a consideration in sitting James and possibly resting Embiid. Philadelphia last played on Tuesday, losing 123-101 to the Boston Celtics in the hyped first meeting between former teammates Jaylen Brown and Jayson Tatum.

However, the Sixers do play back-to-back games on Sunday and Monday, hosting the Indiana Pacers then visiting the Brooklyn Nets.

So far this season, James is averaging 15.1 points, 7.2 rebounds and 6.5 assists on 43% shooting from the floor. Embiid is scoring 17.7 points per game with 9.3 rebounds and 3.8 assists. He is also shooting 37%, while making only 4 of 33 (12%) 3-point attempts.

If Embiid hadn't played, Philadelphia would be short-handed at center with Adem Bona (cervical spine sprain) and Dominick Barlow (low back stress reaction) also out for Thursday. Perhaps that influenced the decision to play him against the Raptors.

James started at center when Embiid was sidelined on Oct. 25 versus the Detroit Pistons. Had Embiid been out, the Sixers would have faced going small with 6-foot-7 Jabari Walker in the middle, or perhaps playing 7-foot-6 Tacko Fall for only the second time this season.

articles.title: Ex-NBA player Gilbert Arenas responds to Steph Curry, stands by calling wife Ayesha a family 'blemish'
articles.summary: Gilbert Arenas offered a conditional apology on his podcast after Steph Curry posted a video defending Ayesha Curry against critical comments.
articles.body: Former Golden State Warriors player Gilbert Arenas clarified his comments about current Warriors star Stephen Curry’s wife, Ayesha, but stopped short of offering a full apology. Speaking on his "Gil’s Arena" podcast, Arenas said his comments were intended to point out that Steph typically avoids controversy while identifying what he called a "blemish" on the Curry family. "All I said is he doesn’t get in trouble for nothing," Arenas said. "He says the right things. If you gotta judge this family, his only blemish is what his wife said. That’s all I said. If there is a blemish, it’s that." The three-time All-Star later expressed regret if his comments offended Steph, but maintained that he had not intended them as a personal attack. Nick Young, who is a "Gil's Arena" contributor, provided a more direct apology. "This man Gil won’t say sorry at all. I’m sorry, Steph. You my dog. I love you. If I offended you, I apologize like a man. I’m sorry," Young said. Young was Curry’s teammate for one season in Golden State, winning the 2018 NBA title with the Warriors. Former NFL player Emmanuel Acho also apologized to the Currys for comments he made on a separate podcast. AYESHA CURRY SAYS HUSBAND STEPH CURRY'S NBA PREGAME HABITS INSPIRED HER MOVIE CHARACTER, RESPONDS TO BACKLASH "When a man humbly comes to you and requests an apology, then you wouldn’t be ignorant to respond with anything else than I’m sorry," Acho said. "Steph, I’m sorry for not just offending you but potentially offending your wife. I’m sorry for how it may have made you feel." Acho added: "I’m sorry for how it may have made you feel seeing headlines, commentary, all these things about your wife," Acho said, referring to the reaction to Ayesha’s starring role in the Roku romantic comedy "Second Chance Holiday." "I’m sorry for the reactions it may have caused internally, vicariously among you, in your central and nervous system." The string of mea culpas came to light shortly after Curry took to social media to address criticism of his wife of 15 years. "Usually the noise doesn’t bother me, it doesn’t bother Ayesha, but this one in particular, when you’re trying to step on the accomplishments of my wife and, you know, obviously needing podcasts, tapings and topics and giving opinions on somebody else’s wife," Curry said in an Instagram video posted on Wednesday. STEPHEN CURRY ISSUES RARE PUBLIC RESPONSE TO CRITICS, DEFENDS WIFE AYESHA AMID ACTING-ROLE BACKLASH One scene in the film calls for Ayesha to kiss co-star Matthew Daddario, a moment that sparked debate and criticism among sports figures on social media. "Nick, Gil, Emmanuel, and anybody else who feels the need to wanna have to, you know, jump in and give an opinion of something you don’t really know about, something that kinda speaks to a bigger conversation on how you view women in this world and what they’re allowed and what they’re not allowed to do." After defending his wife, Curry closed with a pointed thank you to the critics for the unsolicited publicity. ESPN reported Thursday, citing sources, that the Warriors are anticipating the star guard will be sidelined for closer to a month. Curry’s night ended early Wednesday when he left the Warriors’ game against the Houston Rockets with less than seven minutes remaining in the first quarter. He later underwent an MRI.
